rationale: Greek πρὸς ὥραν 'for an hour, for a season' — the temporal-bounded antithesis of ϣⲁⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ 'forever.' Used here to contrast the 'first death' (temporary) with the 'second death' (eternal).
Lyc. reflex of Sahidic ⲥⲱϩⲣ̄ 'drive away, banish, dispel' with 3pl object suffix. Fits eschatological banishment context paralleling ⲡⲱⲣⲭ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'separate forth.'

Likely Lycopolitan orthographic variant of ⲡⲉⲟⲟⲩ 'the glory,' here in apposition to ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'the Light' as the radiance that sheds light upon the cosmos. Construction ⲡⲣⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ ⲁ- 'shines upon' + cosmos-object confirms the appositional reading.

Tentative Lyc. reflex of ⲥⲁⲛⲟⲩϣ 'nourish, rear, feed.' Fits the third element in the triadic separation: stripped of Light (l.8), separated from Air (l.9), no longer nourished by Soul (l.10). Confidence low.

Probable abbreviated compound of ϣⲃ̄ⲓⲁⲓⲧ 'altered, strange' + ⲙⲩⲥⲧⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ. The phrase ⲉⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ϣⲃⲙⲩⲥⲧⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ ⲉⲛ ⲛⲉ ⲙ̄ⲡⲉϩⲥⲁⲩⲛⲉ characterizes the disciples as those for whom no mystery is foreign in his knowledge — fully initiated. Alternative parse as ϣⲃⲏⲣ-ⲙⲩⲥⲧⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ 'fellow-mystery' yields less coherent sense with the negation.
